subject.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)

question: Should OpenClaw expose `capabilities.tts.voice.captionedFinalText` as a supported channel-plugin contract that lets core suppress live final-mode text for caption-capable voice delivery?
rationale: This is a new public plugin capability with user-visible delivery semantics and a failure mode where a mistaken channel declaration can suppress reply text; tests cannot determine whether that is the desired permanent SDK boundary.

options.title: Approve the generic capability
options.body: Accept the opt-in plugin contract, contingent on exact-head Telegram proof for success and fallback behavior.

options.title: Keep the behavior Telegram-owned
options.body: Avoid a new shared channel contract and move the captioned-delivery policy into the Telegram plugin until a broader API need is established.

options.title: Defer the contract
options.body: Pause this PR while maintainers define the broader multi-channel TTS caption capability and compatibility policy.

recommendation.title: Approve the generic capability
recommendation.body: Accept the opt-in plugin contract, contingent on exact-head Telegram proof for success and fallback behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The review timeline provides the strongest available signal of involvement in the initial decision surface, though repository history could not be re-read in this read-only environment.
